package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling logic, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes, leading to account hijacking, web content injection, page defacement, and redirection attacks. The vulnerabilities stem from inconsistent sanitization between client-side and server-side code, and insufficient attribute whitelisting.

execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (FigCaption widget, client-side)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user pastes this payload into the CKEditor in source mode, the code injects a <script> tag into the caption, which is executed in preview mode, resulting in a self-XSS alert.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting <script> tags into user-editable fields should be sanitized to prevent XSS. The ability to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser is a critical security risk.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or escape script tags in captions. Here, the preview mode fails to sanitize, allowing script execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; script injection in captions is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Presence of <script> tags in user-supplied input
Execution of JavaScript in preview mode

execution_context.trigger: content render-time (after storage, on page view)
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor FigCaption widget, rendered HTML in Drupal page

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When rendered, this code injects an <a> tag with a class that covers the entire page, making any click redirect the user to an attacker-controlled site.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting classes that manipulate the entire page layout and redirect users is a classic phishing/defacement technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal captions should not allow arbitrary classes or full-page overlays. Here, the lack of attribute whitelisting allows abuse.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of classes for styling, but not for full-page overlays or redirection.
key_indicators: Use of classes like 'joyride-modal-bg' to cover UI

execution_context.trigger: content render-time (widget rehydration in editor or page view)
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor widget HTML, with data-* attributes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the widget is rehydrated in the editor, the data-cke-widget-data JSON is parsed and used to set the src attribute of the tag, allowing a javascript: URL to be injected and potentially executed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing widget data to set critical attributes like src without proper scheme validation enables XSS via javascript: URLs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal widget data should be sanitized and not allow dangerous URL schemes. Here, the widget logic trusts unsanitized data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of data-* attributes for widget state, but not for setting executable code.
key_indicators: src attributes set to javascript: URLs
Widget rehydration logic trusting user input

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts malicious HTML payload using FigCaption or widget attributes (e.g., script injection, malicious classes, or javascript: URLs).
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in Drupal content or previewed in the editor.

attack_chain.action: Payload is rendered in the CKEditor preview or on the Drupal site, triggering DOM manipulation or script execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: XSS is executed, or the page is defaced/redirected.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the victim's browser, leading to account hijacking, phishing, or further exploitation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control or exfiltrates sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of <script> tags or javascript: URLs in data-caption or widget data attributes
Use of classes that overlay or hide page content (e.g., joyride-modal-bg)
Injection of arbitrary attributes or data-* attributes in FigCaption or widget HTML
file_indicators: HTML content in Drupal nodes with suspicious or tags in captions
data-caption attributes containing HTML or script tags
data-cke-widget-data JSON with src or href set to javascript: URLs
network_indicators: Unexpected redirections to external domains from Drupal content
Outbound requests triggered by injected JavaScript in user sessions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Drupal content fields and CKEditor widget data for suspicious HTML, such as <script> tags, javascript: URLs, or classes that manipulate the UI. Monitor for unexpected redirections or DOM changes on page render. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block script injection and validate attribute whitelists in FigCaption and widget logic.
